data.ruling:
The datasheet verifier's refutation stands, on the critical pin hold check. The stock verifier confirmed every figure and refuted nothing.

The function's decided behaviour is in IOBoard.md, Current aborts, and in the Servo current ceiling row (owner, 2026-09-30):
- Each INA3221's Critical output carries the 3.0 A abort.
- The main coprocessor aborts only when the line stays low longer than a blanking time.
- A shorter trip is logged, not an abort.

V287 (for research, owner 2026-10-01) asks for that blanking time against the INA3221's conversion time. Setting it needs one fact: how long the transparent Critical pin stays low under a sustained over-limit current on one channel while three channels convert in turn. SBOS576C does not state this. I re-read the datasheet at its source:
- 7.3.2.1 says only when the pin pulls low.
- Table 8-34 defines CEN = 0 only as "Transparent (default)".
- The only release wording, 7.5.3, applies to Latch mode.
- The application example, 9.2.1 Table 9-1, enables CH1 alone, so Figures 9-2 and 9-3 cannot show how three channels share the pin.

The datasheet does not rule out one reading: the pin follows each conversion of any channel. Under that reading, a sustained fault on one of three shunt-only channels holds the line low for 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum in every 3.3 to 3.63 ms. The cases then fail as follows:
- A blanking time above 1.21 ms never fires, so the 3.0 A abort never happens.
- A blanking time below one conversion blanks nothing, which defeats the owner's logged-not-aborted rule for a servo charging its capacitors.

So the maker's documents cannot show that the part meets the function's abort requirement. A part qualified on that behaviour would rest on an assumption. Two TI E2E threads (TI's support forum), which are secondary sources and not maker figures, leave the point open:
- 807608: a TI engineer says the pin restores "after one conversion", without naming whose. A customer saw Ch.1 low for "6 channels sampled x 8.24ms", with the alert mode not stated.
- 1625525: a TI engineer says the alert clears "as soon as the shunt voltage drops back down", with no multi-channel case.

The FU-2H adjudicator rulings 016 and 017 held the same release point as not read. No owner answer under Raised by P1 has settled it since, and V287 is the last INA3221 entry. Either of two things closes it: a bench measurement of the Critical pin with 3 channels enabled and one over the limit, or TI's statement of the release point. An owner decision that changes the abort scheme would also close it, for example latch mode cleared by the measurement coprocessor, or counting lows in a window. That decision is the owner's, not this ruling's.

The scope is the function. Lifecycle (ACTIVE at TI, Active at Digi-Key), end-of-life notices (none), LCSC identity (C181255) and the S1 (sourcing rule 1) allowlist (Texas Instruments) all pass. The fault is the fit of this function's alert timing.

The relayed V318/V319 question, 18 V in place of 20 V against 27 V, concerns R5's bus. It does not touch this ruling. The port monitors sit on servo rails of 8.4 V at most, and their 26 V input rating passes either way.
data.evidence: SBOS576C (MAY 2012, revised SEPTEMBER 2026). 7.3.2.1: "The Critical alert pin pulls low if any channel measurement exceeds the limit present in the corresponding-channel critical-alert limit register." No sentence states when the pin releases. Table 8-34, bit 10 CEN: "Critical alert latch enable ... 0 = Transparent (default), 1 = Latch enabled". CF1-3 "are cleared when the Mask/Enable register is read back", which says nothing about the pin. 7.5.3: "continues to hold the alert line low until the interrupt is cleared. Alerts must be in Latch mode to function." 9.2.1 Table 9-1: "Enabled channel CH1", operating mode "Shunt voltage, continuous". 9.2.2: "the Critical alert pin pulls low after the conversion cycle completes", for 1.1 ms and 588 us. 6.5: tCONVERT at CT=100 is 1.1 ms typical and 1.21 ms maximum, with no minimum. 7.4.2.1: shunt-only mode on 3 channels puts two other conversions between repeats of one channel. A text search of the datasheet for latch, release, clears and deassert finds no release condition for the transparent Critical pin. TI E2E 807608, TI engineer: "If the Critical pin is set to transparent mode, after the over limit condition is removed, the Critical pin should restore automatically after one conversion." Customer, same thread: "The Critical flag (Ch.1) remains active for 50ms (6 channels sampled x 8.24ms)", with the mode not stated. TI E2E 1625525, TI engineer: "As soon as the shunt voltage drops back down below the programmed level, the alert clears." Neither thread covers three enabled channels. Requirement: IOBoard.md, Current aborts (row at :113) and Servo current ceiling (:389); Research.md V287 (:1000) and the Follow-ups row (:594). Earlier rulings: round2/FU-2H/016-adjudicator-R8-3.json and 017-adjudicator-R8-4.json, both stands true, scope function.
